os-efcore-sqlserver.title: SQL Server
os-efcore-sqlserver.summary: SQL Server and Azure SQL with a safe setup out of the box: an encrypted connection with a checked certificate, SQL Server's own retries, and its error numbers turned into clear results.

gives.1: The connection is encrypted and the server certificate is checked, even if the connection string says otherwise.
gives.2: Temporary failures such as deadlocks and dropped connections are retried by SQL Server's own strategy, and `TranAsync` stays safe under it.
gives.3: A duplicate value, a missing reference or a too-long text comes back with the field name, never with the server's message.

connection.title: Connecting safely
connection.summary: Give a connection string; encryption, certificate checking and retries are set for you.

1.title: Encrypted connection
1.text: The server certificate is checked, even if the connection string asks otherwise.

2.title: Automatic retries
2.text: Deadlocks and dropped connections are retried for you.

4.title: Concurrent edits
4.text: `Versioned()` catches two people editing at the same time.

1.title: Encryption and certificate
1.text:
A connection string copied from an old project may say `Encrypt=False` or `TrustServerCertificate=True`, which sends data in clear text or accepts any certificate. Here the options always win: the connection is encrypted (`Mandatory`) and the certificate is checked.

Relax this only through the options and only where it is safe, for example `TrustServerCertificate = true` for LocalDB on your own machine.

2.title: Retries
2.text:
With `RetryOnFailure` on (the default), temporary failures are retried by SQL Server's retrying strategy, using `RetryCount` and `RetryDelay` from `EFCoreOptions`. Set `RetryCount` to 0 to turn retries off.

The command timeout, the migrations history table and start-up migration also come from `EFCoreOptions`.

3.title: Dates and concurrent edits
3.text: `DateTimeOffset` is stored as `datetimeoffset`, and edits by two people are caught by the core `Versioned()` token, so the same model works on every database.

4.title: A very busy database
4.text: Turning on `READ_COMMITTED_SNAPSHOT` on the database itself reduces blocking between readers and writers. This package does not change database settings.

secure.title: What the connection really uses
secure.note: The string asked for no encryption and a trusted certificate; the options overrode both.

retries.title: Retries and command timeout
retries.note: The context retries temporary failures and gives each command 30 seconds.

type.SqlServerOptions: The connection string and the security and retry switches.

SqlServerOptions.TrustServerCertificate: Accepts any server certificate. Off by default; turn it on only for LocalDB or a development server.

SqlServerEx.AddOSSqlServer: Registers a context on SQL Server. Registers OS.EFCore too when it is not registered yet, so one call is enough; call `AddOSEFCore` as well, before or after, only to change its settings.
SqlServerEx.UseOSSqlServer: Applies the SQL Server setup to a builder.

errors.title: Errors and what was tested
errors.summary: How SQL Server errors turn into results, and an honest note on testing.

1.title: Known numbers
1.text: SQL Server error numbers map to stable `data.*` codes.

2.title: Only real constraints
2.text: 547 counts only for FOREIGN KEY or REFERENCE; a CHECK is `data.error`.

3.title: Private messages
3.text: The server's message is read only to find the field.

4.title: What was tested
4.text: Real-server tests ran on LocalDB; the rest only as unit tests.

1.title: Recognized numbers
1.text:
These SQL Server error numbers are recognized (checked on Microsoft Learn): 2627 and 2601 give `data.duplicate` with the field; 515 gives `data.required`; 547 gives `data.missingRef`, or `data.inUse` when deleting, but only for a FOREIGN KEY or REFERENCE constraint; 2628 and 8152 give `data.tooLong`.

1205 (deadlock), 1222 (lock timeout), ‎-2 (timeout) and 40501 (service busy) give `data.busy`; and 53, ‎-1, 10053, 10054, 10060, 40613 and 40197 give `data.offline`.

2.title: Everything else
2.text: Anything else, including a CHECK constraint, is `data.error`. The server's message is read only to find the field; it never reaches a result.

3.title: What was tested
3.text:
Tests against a real server ran on LocalDB: duplicate, required, too long, missing reference and in use errors, transactions under the retrying strategy, the version token and dates.

Deadlocks, lock timeouts, network and Azure errors and a commit that fails half-way were tested only with unit tests and the core's simulated failures.

save-item.title: Turn a SQL Server result into a message
save-item.note: The same codes as every other database, so this code does not change if the database does.
